question: Natural rubber is soft at high temperatures and brittle at low temperatures; hence raw rubber is heated with sulphur and other additives at a temperature range between 373 – 415 K to make it strong. This process is called ______ of rubber.
solution:
The correct answer is __Vulcanisation**(of rubber)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vulcanisation__ is a chemical process used to strengthen rubber.
 
• It involves heating raw rubber with sulphur and other additives at a temperature range of 373–415 K.
 
• Vulcanisation improves the elasticity, durability, and resistance of rubber to extreme temperatures.
 
• Natural rubber becomes soft at high temperatures and brittle at low temperatures, which is overcome by vulcanisation.
 
• The process was invented by Charles Goodyear in the 19th century.
 
• Vulcanised rubber is used in automobile tires, shoe soles, belts, hoses, and many other products.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Molding:**

 
 
• Molding refers to shaping rubber or other materials by pouring or forcing it into a mold.
 
• It is widely used in manufacturing processes for creating desired shapes.
 
 
 
• **Extrusion:**
 
 
• Extrusion is a process of shaping rubber by forcing it through a die.
 
• It is commonly used to make tubes, pipes, and cables.
 
 
 
• **Latex:**
 
 
• Latex is a milky fluid obtained naturally from rubber trees.
 
• It is processed to produce natural rubber and other products.
